extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and applicants preparing or evaluating 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, filing, and evaluating affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131(a) to antedate references ("swearing behind"), including what evidence is required, when the procedure applies or is inappropriate, and examiner form paragraphs and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim of an application or a patent under reexamination is rejected, the inventor of the subject matter of the rejected claim, the owner of the patent under reexamination, or the party qualified under § 1.42 or § 1.46, may submit an appropriate oath or declaration to establish invention of the subject matter of the rejected claim prior to the effective date of the reference or activity on which the rejection is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior invention may not be established under this section in any country other than the United States, a NAFTA country, or a WTO member country. Prior invention may not be established under this section before December 8, 1993 in a NAFTA country other than the United States, or before January 1, 1996 in a WTO member country other than a NAFTA country. Prior invention may not be established under this section if either (1) the rejection is based upon a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication naming another inventor which claims interfering subject matter (suggest interference instead), or (2) the rejection is based upon a statutory bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of facts required — reduction to practice or conception plus diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing of facts for an oath or declaration shall be such, in character and weight, as to establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, or conception of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference coupled with due diligence from prior to said date to a subsequent reduction to practice or to the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, must accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or their absence must be satisfactorily explained. Conception must be proved (not a vague idea) — e.g., demonstrative evidence or complete disclosure to another. See case law referenced (e.g., Mergenthaler v. Scudder) for explanation of what constitutes conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) to disqualify commonly owned patent for 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 on a U.S. patent or publication that is not prior art under 102(b) and the inventions are not identical but not patentably distinct and are owned by the same party, the applicant may disqualify the patent/publication as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To disqualify the patent/publication the applicant must submit (1) a terminal disclaimer in accordance with § 1.321(c); and (2) an oath or declaration stating current common ownership and that the inventor named in the examined application is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104 (as in effect on March 15, 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — which applications/patents 1.131 applies to
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions apply to any application for patent, and to any patent issuing thereon, that contains (1) a claim to an invention that has an effective filing date before March 16, 2013; or (2) a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to any patent or application that itself contains a claim with an effective filing date before March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where § 1.130 applies (AIA-era exceptions), § 1.131 applicability is limited only to rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g). See MPEP cross-references for AIA-era practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case — antedating a reference that qualifies under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations may be used to antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 102(b), e.g., where the prior art date of the reference is less than one year prior to the effective filing date of the applicant’s claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference under 102(a) is a U.S. patent or application publication, the reference may not be antedated if it claims interfering subject matter as defined in 37 CFR 41.203(a). See MPEP § 715.05 for interfering subject matter discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case — antedating a reference under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations may be used to antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), where the reference has a 102(e) prior art date prior to the effective filing date of applicant’s claimed invention and shows but does not claim interfering subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2136‑2136.03 for what references qualify under pre-AIA 102(e) and MPEP § 715.05 for interfering subject matter discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case — antedating an activity under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination, an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) may antedate an activity that qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) (and not under 102(b)), e.g., where the prior art date of the activity is less than one year prior to the effective filing date of applicant’s claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the activity evidence is a U.S. patent or application publication, it may not be antedated if it claims interfering subject matter as defined in 37 CFR 41.203(a). See MPEP § 715.05 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — application subject to current 35 U.S.C. 102 (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is not appropriate where the application is subject to current 35 U.S.C. 102 and the affidavit is not directed to evidence used in a rejection based on pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate AIA-era provisions (e.g., 1.130) for first-inventor-to-file situations unless relying on pre-AIA 102(g) grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — statutory bar (reference publication date > 1 year) (B)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is not appropriate where the reference publication date is more than one year prior to the effective filing date of the claimed invention — such reference is a statutory bar under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reference that only qualifies under 102(a) or 102(e) is not a 'statutory bar' for this purpose; the >1 year publication-date bar is the key exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — reference claims interfering subject matter (C)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration is inappropriate where the reference U.S. patent or application publication claims interfering subject matter as defined in 37 CFR 41.203(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference and application are not commonly owned, the reference can only be overcome by establishing priority of invention through interference proceedings. If commonly owned, use 1.131(c) procedures. See MPEP § 715.05 and Chapter 2300.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — foreign patent to same invention filed >12 months before domestic filing (D)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131(a) is not appropriate where the reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant or patent owner (or their legal representatives/assigns) issued prior to the filing date of the domestic application on an application filed more than 12 months prior to the filing date of the domestic application (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such foreign filings create bars that cannot be antedated under 1.131(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — unnecessary when applicant’s effective filing date is prior to reference (E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the effective filing date of applicant’s or patent owner's claimed invention is prior to the effective date of the reference, an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is unnecessary because the reference should not have been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP §§ 211‑216 for related practice and handling of such references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — statutory double patenting (F)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is inappropriate where the reference patent or application publication claims the same invention and the claimed invention under examination is subject to statutory double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 804 for double patenting issues and resolution (terminal disclaimers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — applicant’s clear admission on the record (G)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is inappropriate where applicant has clearly admitted on the record that the subject matter relied on in the rejection is prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions on the record may not be overcome by an affidavit/declaration under 1.131. See cited cases (In re Hellsund, In re Garfinkel, In re Blout, In re Lopresti) for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — subject matter is prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) (H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131(a) are inappropriate where the subject matter relied upon is prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 102(f) deals with work of others; affidavits claiming earlier invention by applicant cannot overcome a true 102(f) showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate — lost count in interference / interference estoppel issues (I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits are inappropriate where the subject matter corresponding to a lost count in an interference is either prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) or barred to applicant by doctrine of interference estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cited cases (In re Bandel, In re Kroekel, In re Deckler, In re Zletz) and MPEP §§ 2138.01 and 2138.02 for nuances (there are circumstances where a losing party may still use 1.131 if the newly claimed invention is not 'substantially the same').

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date to be overcome — US patents, US application publications, and international publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art). For domestic patents used as references under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) the effective date is the earlier of the actual filing date of the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application and the earliest claimed domestic benefit date that the reference is entitled to, but not the foreign priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Hilmer supports that foreign filing date is not the relevant effective date when used as a reference under pre-AIA 102(e). See MPEP §§ 2136‑2136.03 for detailed rules on effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date to be overcome — foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign patents the date of availability as prior art is governed by the rules in MPEP §§ 2126‑2127.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult those MPEP sections for determination of when a foreign patent becomes available as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date to be overcome — printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed publication, including a published foreign patent application, is effective as of its publication date, not its date of receipt by the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2128‑2128.02 for additional information regarding effective dates of printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date to be overcome — activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For activities relied on (e.g., public use, sales, knowledge by others), the effective date of the activity used to reject the claims is the date the activity was first known to have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2120.02 and 2133.03 for handling activities and determining their effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs — general usage (7.57.fti–7.64.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.57.fti through 7.64.fti may be used by examiners to respond to 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavits and declarations to indicate insufficiency, the insufficiency basis, or sufficiency to overcome a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph has specific bracketed insertions and sequencing requirements (e.g., 7.57.fti must precede others when indicating ineffective; some paragraphs require explanatory text in brackets). Examiners must follow the stated 'Examiner Note' instructions for sequencing and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.57.fti — Affidavit/Declaration Under 37 CFR 1.131(a): Ineffective — Heading
rubrics_metrics.description: The filed affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) has been considered but is ineffective to overcome the [reference].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket instructions: insert either '--affidavit--' or '--declaration--' and follow with one or more of form paragraphs 7.58.fti to 7.63.fti or a paragraph setting forth the proper basis for insufficiency (e.g., failure to establish acts performed in this country, scope not commensurate with claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.58.fti — Ineffective: Claiming Same Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The [reference] is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication of a pending or patented application that claims the rejected invention. An affidavit or declaration is inappropriate under 37 CFR 1.131(a) when the reference is claiming interfering subject matter as defined in 37 CFR 41.203(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference and this application are not commonly owned, the reference can only be overcome by interference proceedings; if commonly owned, may be disqualified via 1.131(c). Examiner Note: must be preceded by 7.57.fti when used to respond to an affidavit; may also be used alone to inform applicant that an affidavit would be inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.59.fti — Ineffective: Insufficient Evidence of Reduction to Practice Before Reference Date
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish a reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA or WTO member country prior to the effective date of the [reference].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57.fti. Examiner must provide an explanation of the lack of showing in the bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.60.fti — Ineffective: Reference Is a Statutory Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The [reference] is a statutory bar under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and thus cannot be overcome by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.61.fti — Ineffective: Insufficient Evidence of Conception
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish a conception of the invention prior to the effective date of the [reference].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception is the mental part of the inventive act and must be provable (e.g., demonstrative evidence or complete disclosure to another). Must be preceded by 7.57.fti. If affidavit also fails to establish diligence or reduction to practice, follow with 7.62.fti and/or 7.63.fti as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.62.fti — Ineffective: Diligence Lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish diligence from a date prior to the date of reduction to practice of the [reference] to either a constructive reduction to practice or an actual reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57.fti. If conception also lacking, 7.61.fti must precede. If affidavit establishes conception, the examiner should state that. See MPEP § 715.07(a) — diligence is not required after reduction to practice. Provide explanation in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.63.fti — Ineffective: Insufficient Evidence of Actual Reduction to Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish the inventor’s alleged actual reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA or WTO member country after the effective date of the [reference].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57.fti. If alleged reduction to practice is prior to the effective date of the reference do not use this paragraph (use 7.59.fti instead). If affidavit also fails to establish conception or diligence, include 7.61.fti and/or 7.62.fti as well. Explain deficiency in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.64.fti — Effective To Overcome Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The [affidavit/declaration] filed on [date] under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is sufficient to overcome the [reference].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert '--affidavit--' or '--declaration--' in bracket 1, the filing date in bracket 2, and the name of the reference in bracket 3. Examiner should record that the affidavit/declaration has been accepted and the rejection withdrawn (note: the rejection is withdrawn, not the reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 vs affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit/declaration is to overcome a prior art rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 by proving invention by the inventor prior to the effective date of the reference. Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132 traverse rejections by proving inventorship or attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits submitted under 1.131 when they are actually aimed at establishing that the reference discloses the inventor's invention (i.e., proper 1.132 purpose) will be treated as though filed under 1.132. See MPEP § 715.01. For practice under AIA-era exceptions, see MPEP §§ 717 and 2155.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference naming different inventive entity with at least one common inventor — 1.131 vs 1.132 considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When subject matter disclosed in a patent or publication naming an inventive entity including joint inventor S and another joint inventor is claimed in a later application naming sole inventor S without the joint inventor, the reference may be applied until overcome by an affidavit/declaration under 1.131(a) showing prior invention or by an affidavit/declaration under 1.132 traversing the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A naked assertion of inventorship by a joint inventor (without context, explanation, or corroborating evidence) is insufficient (see EmeraChem v. Volkswagen). If reference is a domestic patent/publication that includes a claim reciting the relied-upon subject matter, a 1.132 declaration must explain the presence of the additional joint inventor. Testimony or disclaimer from other joint inventors is usually not required but should be considered if submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make affidavit/declaration and formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor of the subject matter, the owner of the patent under reexamination, or the party qualified under § 1.42 or § 1.46 may submit an appropriate oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements include proper oath or declaration wording and accompanying exhibits (originals or photocopies) that become part of the affidavit/declaration. Where an affidavit is improperly filed under 1.131 but is actually a submission under 1.132, it will be considered under 1.132. See MPEP §§ 715.04 and 717 for formality and AIA-era distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts and documentary evidence — diligence, interference testimony, country-of-acts, disposition of exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations must be supported by facts and documentary evidence addressing conception, reduction to practice, and diligence. Acts relied upon must have been carried out in the United States or a NAFTA/WTO member country as applicable. Original exhibits should accompany the submission; disposition of exhibits is governed by MPEP rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.07(a)-(d) for details: (a) diligence rules (diligence is not required after reduction to practice), (b) interference testimony sometimes used, (c) acts relied upon must be in eligible countries, and (d) disposition procedures for exhibits. Explanations for missing originals must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of presentation — when affidavits/declarations may be filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131(a) must be presented seasonably; certain late filings may be permitted in narrow circumstances (e.g., with an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 in utility/plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995 or a CPA under 1.53(d) in design applications), but generally cannot be filed after prosecution is closed unless conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All admitted affidavits and declarations are acknowledged and commented upon by the examiner in the next action. Review of an examiner’s refusal to enter an affidavit as untimely is by petition, not appeal (see In re Deters and Ex parte Hale). See MPEP § 715.09 for timeliness rules and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review for prior public use/on sale and best mode (715.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review affidavits/declarations and accompanying evidence carefully to determine whether they show that the claimed invention was 'in public use' or 'on sale' in this country more than one year prior to the effective filing date (statutory bar under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the affidavit antedates the reference, applicant’s own prior public use or sale may create a statutory bar that cannot be overcome by 1.131(a). Where the affidavit relies on an embodiment not disclosed in the application, an examiner must consider whether the best mode requirement is violated and should only make a best mode rejection if the record establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that the specification fails to set forth the best mode contemplated (see MPEP §§ 2165‑2165.04).
